outcome: Redington consolidates virtual machines and containers onto one platform, so the estate needs a single operating model instead of two.
overview: Manufacturers reviewing their virtualisation licensing find the same obstacle: most workloads could move to containers eventually, but a long tail of virtual machines — line-of-business applications, vendor appliances, controllers nobody may touch — cannot. Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization runs those virtual machines on the same platform as the containers, so the estate consolidates onto one control plane without waiting for the tail to be rewritten. It buys time and removes a second licensing relationship. Redington sizes the new platform from measured capacity and migrates a named first wave of machines before anything larger is committed.

benefits.text: Virtual machines and containers run on one platform, so the estate needs one operating model rather than two
benefits.limits: Only for machines whose guest operating systems and device requirements the platform supports; the exceptions must be found in assessment, not at cutover

benefits.text: A second virtualisation licensing relationship can be ended rather than renewed
benefits.limits: Real only if the incumbent is fully retired; a partial migration leaves both contracts in place and costs more, not less

benefits.text: Workloads that cannot be containerised stop blocking the platform decision
benefits.limits: The tail still has to be operated; this removes the platform obstacle, not the maintenance burden

residency: Entirely on customer-owned infrastructure; virtual machine images and their data never leave the customer data centre

notFor.situation: An estate with no container workloads and no plan to acquire any
notFor.why: Running virtual machines on a container platform is only worth the change when both kinds of workload share it

notFor.situation: Virtual machines with specialised hardware passthrough the platform does not support
notFor.why: Device dependencies are the most common reason a migration stalls after commitment

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Red Hat implementation partner · Duration: 12–16 weeks to a migrated first wave, hardware lead time excluded
Support model: Vendor subscription support for the platform; Redington coordinates the vendor case and holds the migration relationship.
1) Assessment — machine inventory, measured capacity, guest-support check and the exception list
2) Design — target sizing, storage and network integration, migration waves and rollback
3) Build — bare-metal cluster, storage, virtualisation enablement and the import path
4) Migrate and hand over — first wave migrated and validated, operations handed to the customer team
deliverables: A migrated machine runs with its disks intact and meets the performance profile recorded in assessment
Virtual machines and containers are managed through one console and one policy set
The customer team completes a machine migration from the incumbent unaided
effort: 12–16 weeks to a migrated first wave, hardware lead time excluded
languages: English delivery; Arabic executive materials on request
